sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Fluo-4 Ca2+ assay: myc-tagged WT EC50 = 670 nM vs untagged WT EC50 = 772 nM; equivalent response, function preserved. Surface expression confirmed by ELISA.
sites.rationale: GPR139 has no endogenous signal peptide (topology is extracellular from residue 1), so the N-terminal extracellular face is the sole extracellular terminus; insert_after_residue=0 places the tag before M1. The position is topology-derived: no residue number is named in any ledger line, but there is exactly one extracellular terminus. Three independent papers using three different tag types (c-myc, V5, HA) all converge on this same junction, and L4 demonstrates functionally equivalent Ca2+ signaling (EC50 ratio 0.87), confirming the tag is tolerated without impairing Gq coupling. N-terminally c-myc-tagged full-length human GPR139 (NM_001002911.3) expressed in HEK cells using pEGFP-N1 vector with an exogenous mGluR5 signal peptide (cleaved post-translationally) followed by c-myc before GPR139 residue 1; surface expression confirmed by ELISA. Corroborated by two additional papers: V5-tagged GPR139 (PMC6367278, L5/L6) and HA-tagged GPR139 with HA signal peptide (PMC12287315, L7), all placing a tag at the same N-terminal extracellular junction.

sources.claim: The myc-tagged wild-type (WT) receptor displayed equivalent response to 1a in the Fluo-4 Ca 2+ -assay (EC 50 = 670 nM) as compared to the untagged WT receptor (EC 50 = 772 nM) (Supplementary Fig. 2 ).

literature_notes: All seven ledger lines describe N-terminal extracellular tags on full-length GPR139; no ledger line supports an internal loop insertion or a C-terminal tag. The three extracellular loops (ECL1: 87-102, ECL2: 166-181, ECL3: 250-264) have no ledger support and are not proposed. No ledger line reports an intracellular tag or a function-abrogating insertion, so other_positions is empty. The exogenous signal peptides (mGluR5 SP in L2, HA SP in L7) are construct elements cleaved before the tag reaches the cell surface; they do not shift the GPR139 residue numbering.
